stem.text: X and Y are sodium salts of Group 17 elements.
When X reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid, hydrogen sulfide, $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, is produced.
When Y reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid, there is no change in the oxidation number of the sulfur.

B.text: Aqueous Y reacts with aqueous silver nitrate to give a precipitate which is insoluble in concentrated aqueous ammonia.

C.text: X and Y react separately with concentrated sulfuric acid to produce halogens.

D.text: When X reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid, six halide ions are needed to reduce one sulfur atom to $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.
